subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Temptation Bundling
description: A micro-lesson that makes Temptation Bundling usable.

hook.text: Only listen to your favorite podcast while exercising. Suddenly the gym isn't a chore — it's the only place you get.

buildup.text: Milkman's temptation bundling pairs a desirable activity with a beneficial but unappealing one.

discovery.text: Applied to finance: review your budget only at your favorite cafe. Transfer savings before buying yourself a treat.

twist.text: The bundle works because the brain merges both activities. Reward from the treat fuels the task.

climax.text: Identify your guilty pleasures. Pair each with a financial task. The pleasure becomes the incentive for the disciplined.

punchline.text: Pair fun with finance. Both get done.

quiz.question: How does temptation bundling work?
options: By pairing a desirable activity with a beneficial but unappealing one
By making all activities equally boring

details.summary: Temptation bundling pairs an enjoyable activity with a beneficial but less appealing one. Allowing yourself to listen to a favorite podcast only while exercising, or watching a show only while doing chores, uses present bias to motivate disciplined behavior.
details.whyItMatters: Temptation bundling converts present bias from an obstacle into an ally. Instead of fighting the desire for immediate gratification, it harnesses that desire to motivate behaviors that produce long-term benefits.
takeaways: Pairing guilty pleasures with healthy habits increases compliance with both
Temptation bundling uses present bias as motivation rather than fighting it
The technique works for exercise, saving, studying, and other discipline challenges

faq.question: What is a practical example of temptation bundling?
faq.answer: Katherine Milkman's study let participants access addictive audiobooks only at the gym. Gym attendance increased by 51 percent because the temptation of the next chapter pulled people to exercise. The want motivates the should.

faq.question: Can temptation bundling help with financial goals?
faq.answer: Yes. You can bundle saving with a reward, like transferring money to savings before allowing a treat. Or pair financial education podcasts with enjoyable activities. The key is making the desired behavior the gateway to the tempting experience.
